newsitem.title: USA: Rainforest to take charge for development.
newsitem.headline: Rainforest to take charge for development.

text.p: Rainforest Cafe Inc said Monday it will take a pretax charge of about $1.9 million, or $0.07 a share after tax, to write off development costs related to previously planned units at Trump Taj Mahal in Atlantic City, New Jersey and Stratosphere in Las Vegas, Nevada.
Rainforest said the non-recurring charge reflects the uncertainty surrounding the company's plan to develop these units.

At Trump Taj Mahal, a Trump Hotels & Casino Resorts Inc development, third-party regulatory restrictions relating to the planned construction over the boardwalk will terminate Rainforest's plans unless these issues can be resolved satisfactorily, Rainforest said.
At Stratosphere Corp's Las Vegas complex, development of space planned for Rainforest Case has been delayed for some time, it added.
Rainforest said it is not anticipated that this space will be delivered within the required period, resulting in termination of the lease at Stratosphere.
In other developments, Rainforest said its cafe at Aventura Mall in Miami is now scheduled to open in the fourth quarter of 1997, two quarters ahead of schedule.
Its accelerated 1997 schedule brings the total number of Rainforest Cafes planned for 1997 to 10, including eight domestic units and two international.
The company said development of all other units is moving forward as planned.

"We expect to replace the Taj Mahal unit in our 1998 development schedule with one of the many opportunities which exist both domestically and internationally," Martin O'Dowd, Rainforest president, said in a statement.
Rainforest Cafe develops, owns and operates combined restaurant/retail facilities with a rain forest theme.
